items.title: takumi-py
items.text:
Python 3.11+ bindings for the Takumi Rust renderer. Turn typed node trees, HTML, or Jinja templates into raster images, SVG, and animation without a browser runtime.

Get started API reference

Testing-stage project

Public APIs, exception types, and release platforms may still change as Takumi core evolves. Read the changelog before upgrading.

items.title: Minimal example
items.text:
from pathlib import Path

from takumi_py import Renderer

png = Renderer().render_html(
    '<main class="card">Hello from Python</main>',
    stylesheets=[
        """
        .card {
          width: 1200px;
          height: 630px;
          display: flex;
          align-items: center;
          justify-content: center;
          color: white;
          background: #111827;
          font-size: 72px;
        }
        """
    ],  # (1)!
    width=1200,
    height=630,  # (2)!
)

Path("out.png").write_bytes(png)
  1. Document-level CSS is an explicit input. Inline style attributes remain part of the HTML input.
  2. An explicit viewport makes output dimensions deterministic. Either dimension can also be inferred from layout.

items.title: Design boundary
items.text: The binding exposes practical Takumi core capabilities while keeping resource ownership explicit: callers provide external fonts and image bytes, and the renderer does not access the network. The package intentionally has no Playwright fallback, remote fetcher, AbortSignal abstraction, data URL helper, or Node.js sidecar. See the complete support matrix.

items.title: Getting started
items.text:
Follow the shortest path to a working render, then branch into the guide that matches your input and output model.

  • 1. Install

    Use a published wheel or prepare a source checkout with the Takumi submodule.

    Installation

  • 2. Render

    Generate a deterministic PNG from HTML and an explicit stylesheet.

    Quickstart

  • 3. Go deeper

    Select the rendering, resource, template, or animation guide for your workload.

    Browse guides

Using custom text or images?

Read Fonts and images immediately after the quickstart when you need non-Latin text, brand fonts, or in-memory images. The bundled Geist face is a Latin last-resort font, not a general-purpose font collection.

items.title: Installation
items.text:
takumi-py requires Python 3.11 or later. Choose a published wheel for normal use or a source checkout when developing the binding.

PyPISource checkout

Add the binding to a project with uv:

uv add takumi-py

Other standards-compliant Python package managers also work. See the support matrix for the published wheel platforms.

A source build requires Rust 1.91 or later, Python 3.11+, and uv. Takumi is a Git submodule, so clone it recursively:

git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/BalconyJH/takumi-py.git
cd takumi-py
uv sync --all-groups --all-extras
uv run maturin develop

For an existing non-recursive checkout, initialize the submodule first:

git submodule update --init --recursive

items.title: Verify the installation
items.text:
uv run python -c "from takumi_py import Renderer; print(Renderer())"

Self-contained distributions

The source distribution contains the Takumi workspace and default font sources required to rebuild the native extension. Published wheels embed the default font in the extension and do not depend on font files in the runtime working directory.

items.title: Quickstart
items.text:
This program renders HTML with an explicit stylesheet and writes a PNG:

from pathlib import Path

from takumi_py import Renderer

renderer = Renderer()
png = renderer.render_html(
    '<section class="card"><h1>Hello</h1></section>',
    stylesheets=[
        """
        .card {
          width: 1200px;
          height: 630px;
          display: flex;
          align-items: center;
          justify-content: center;
          color: white;
          background: #111827;
        }
        h1 { font-size: 72px; }
        """
    ],  # (1)!
    width=1200,
    height=630,  # (2)!
)

Path("out.png").write_bytes(png)
  1. Stylesheets are passed as document-level render inputs, rather than hidden global renderer state.
  2. Fix both viewport dimensions when the output must be repeatable across calls.

items.title: Choose an input model
items.text:
• HTML already exists: use render_html; see HTML and CSS.
  • Content is structured data: use render_node; see node trees.
  • The same structure is rendered repeatedly: call compile_node or compile_html, then follow the compiled rendering contract.
  • Templates live on disk: use TemplateRenderer; see Jinja templates.

items.title: Next steps
items.text:
The result does not look right

Check these boundaries first:

  1. Are the viewport dimensions explicit or intentionally inferred?
  2. Was document-level CSS passed through stylesheets?
  3. Were the fonts required by the text registered?

Continue with the rendering model and resource guide for the underlying contracts.

items.title: Animation
items.text:
The animation API supports two models: sampling CSS or structured keyframes at a specific time, and encoding a sequence of scenes or raw frames.

flowchart LR
    A["CSS or structured keyframes"] --> S["Sample timeline"]
    B["AnimationScene sequence"] --> F["Render frames"]
    C["RawAnimationFrame sequence"] --> E["Encode"]
    S --> F --> E
    E --> W["WebP"]
    E --> P["APNG"]
    E --> G["GIF"]

items.title: Timeline sampling
items.text:
time_ms selects the instant at which CSS animations are sampled. Keyframes come from @keyframes rules in a stylesheet or from the structured keyframes option:

CSS keyframesStructured keyframes 
from takumi_py import Renderer

frame = Renderer().render_html(
    '<div class="box"></div>',
    stylesheets=[
        """
        @keyframes fade {
          from { opacity: 0; }
          to { opacity: 1; }
        }
        .box {
          width: 64px;
          height: 64px;
          background: black;
          animation: fade 1000ms both;
        }
        """
    ],
    width=64,
    height=64,
    time_ms=500,
)

from takumi_py import Renderer

frame = Renderer().render_node(
    {"type": "container", "className": "box"},
    stylesheets=[
        ".box { width: 64px; height: 64px; animation: fade 1000ms both; }",
    ],
    keyframes={
        "fade": {
            "from": {"opacity": 0},
            "to": {"opacity": 1},
        }
    },
    width=64,
    height=64,
    time_ms=500,
)

RenderOptions(keyframes=...) carries the same structured keyframes, so a reusable options value can hold the animation definition alongside time_ms.

items.title: Scene sequences
items.text:
render_animation accepts a sequence of AnimationScene values, each a node with a duration. The format argument selects WebP, APNG, or GIF, while fps controls how often the timeline is sampled:

from takumi_py import AnimationScene, Renderer

animation = Renderer().render_animation(
    [
        AnimationScene(
            {
                "type": "container",
                "style": {
                    "width": "100%",
                    "height": "100%",
                    "backgroundColor": "black",
                },
            },
            duration_ms=200,
        ),
        AnimationScene(
            {
                "type": "container",
                "style": {
                    "width": "100%",
                    "height": "100%",
                    "backgroundColor": "white",
                },
            },
            duration_ms=200,
        ),
    ],
    width=64,
    height=64,
    fps=20,
    format="webp",
)

render_animation streams each frame into the encoder as it renders, so it holds one raw frame at a time rather than the whole animation. To render a single frame of a sequence instead, call render_sequence_at_time(scenes, time_ms), which returns a static image in any raster format.

items.title: Raw frames
items.text:
Use encode_frames with RawAnimationFrame values when frames are produced elsewhere, for example by format="raw" renders or another image library:

from takumi_py import RawAnimationFrame, Renderer

black = bytes([0, 0, 0, 255] * 4)
white = bytes([255, 255, 255, 255] * 4)

gif = Renderer().encode_frames(
    [
        RawAnimationFrame(black, width=2, height=2, duration_ms=100),
        RawAnimationFrame(white, width=2, height=2, duration_ms=100),
    ],
    format="gif",
)

items.title: Contracts
items.text:
• Every AnimationScene.duration_ms and RawAnimationFrame.duration_ms must be a positive integer. Zero-duration scenes or frames raise ValueError rather than being silently skipped.
  • fps must be positive and must not exceed the delay precision of the selected format: WebP and APNG support at most 90 fps, while GIF supports at most 50 fps. render_animation raises ValueError before rendering when fps is higher.
  • webp_speed, when provided, must be an integer from 0 through 6.
  • A raw frame must have positive dimensions and exactly width * height * 4 RGBA bytes.
  • loop_count sets the number of repetitions; None keeps the format's default.

WebP defaults to lossless

WebP animation defaults to lossless when neither quality nor lossless is specified. quality and lossless=True are mutually exclusive.

See the runnable examples/render_animation.py example.

items.title: HTML and CSS
items.text: Takumi's Rust parser turns HTML into the same node tree that render_node accepts. The binding has no browser and no Python-side HTML parser.

items.title: Render HTML
items.text:
from takumi_py import Renderer

png = Renderer().render_html(
    '<div class="card"><h1>Hello</h1></div>',
    stylesheets=[
        """
        .card {
          width: 1200px;
          height: 630px;
          display: flex;
          align-items: center;
          justify-content: center;
          color: white;
          background: #111827;
        }
        """
    ],
    width=1200,
    height=630,
)

measure_html and render_svg_html accept the same HTML and stylesheet inputs.

items.title: Document structure
items.text:
A source that starts with a doctype or an <html> element parses as a document, with <html>, <head>, and <body> as a browser builds them. Anything else parses as a fragment. A fragment with several top-level elements is wrapped in a container that fills the viewport.

The parser maps style, class, id, dir, lang, and Tailwind attributes onto the node tree. <style> elements and other elements that do not render are dropped, and an <img> without a src renders as an empty box sized by its width and height.

items.title: Stylesheets
items.text:
Inline style attributes are part of the HTML. Document-level CSS is always an explicit input through stylesheets=[...]; <style> elements in the markup are ignored.

HTML and node entry points compile stylesheets differently:

Entry points Compilation Unsupported declaration render_html, measure_html, render_svg_html, render_template, render_svg_template Error-tolerant, like a browser Skipped render_node, measure_node, render_svg_node, render_animation, render_sequence_at_time Strict Raises StyleSheetError

For the compiled APIs, choose explicitly: compile_stylesheet is strict and compile_stylesheet_lossy is error-tolerant.

from takumi_py import Renderer, StyleSheetError

renderer = Renderer()
tolerant = renderer.compile_stylesheet_lossy("a { display: weird; } b { color: red; }")

try:
    renderer.compile_stylesheet("a { display: weird; }")
except StyleSheetError as error:
    print(error)

items.title: Parser options
items.text:
HtmlOptions controls the parser:

from takumi_py import HtmlOptions, Renderer

png = Renderer().render_html(
    '<div class="w-[1200px] h-[630px]"></div>',
    html_options=HtmlOptions(
        presets="none",
        tailwind_property="class",
        max_depth=64,
    ),
    width=None,
    height=None,
)
Option Default Effect presets "chromium" "chromium" applies Chromium's default element styles; "none" applies none tailwind_property None Attribute that carries Tailwind classes; None reads the tw attribute max_depth None Maximum element nesting; None uses Takumi's limit of 512

Nesting deeper than max_depth raises HtmlParseError.

items.title: Parse once, render many
items.text:
parse_html parses without a renderer and returns a ParsedHtml bundle; Renderer.compile_html returns the equivalent CompiledHtml. Pass the bundle's node and stylesheets to the compiled APIs as described in Compile and reuse:

from takumi_py import Renderer, parse_html

parsed = parse_html("<article>Hello</article>")
png = Renderer().render_compiled(
    parsed.node,
    stylesheets=parsed.stylesheets,
    width=320,
    height=160,
)

items.title: Discover external resources
items.text:
The renderer never fetches anything. CompiledNode.resource_urls() lists the HTTP(S) image references in image nodes and styles, so the application can fetch them first:

from takumi_py import Renderer

compiled = Renderer().compile_node(
    {"type": "image", "src": "https://example.com/logo.png"}
)

print(compiled.resource_urls())

It does not report sources the caller already supplied, such as memory:// resources or byte buffers. Pass fetched bytes back as ImageResource values, as described in Fonts and images.

See the runnable examples/render_html.py example.

items.title: Output formats
items.text:
Every input renders to the same set of outputs:

Output API family Result PNG, JPEG, WebP, ICO render_* Encoded bytes Raw RGBA render_* with format="raw" Pixel bytes SVG render_svg_* str Layout only measure_* MeasuredNode WebP, APNG, GIF animation render_animation, encode_frames Encoded bytes; see Animation

items.title: Raster images
items.text:
format selects the encoder; "png" is the default.

from takumi_py import Renderer

jpeg = Renderer().render_html(
    "<h1>Hello</h1>",
    width=320,
    height=160,
    format="jpeg",
    quality=90,
)
Format Encoder options "png" None "jpeg" or "jpg" quality from 0 through 100, default 75 "webp" Lossless unless quality is set; lossless=True cannot be combined with quality "ico" None

device_pixel_ratio scales CSS lengths into output pixels. At 2.0, a 10px box covers 20 output pixels. An explicit width and height set the canvas size in output pixels, while an inferred dimension scales with the content.

dithering="ordered-bayer" dithers gradient fills before they are quantized to 8 bits, which reduces banding in smooth gradients.

items.title: Raw RGBA
items.text:
format="raw" skips encoding and returns row-major RGBA bytes with straight alpha, 4 bytes per pixel:

from takumi_py import Renderer

raw = Renderer().render_node(
    {
        "type": "container",
        "style": {"width": "24px", "height": "12px", "backgroundColor": "white"},
    },
    width=None,
    height=None,
    format="raw",
)

assert len(raw) == 24 * 12 * 4

Raw output pairs with encode_frames for animations assembled in Python, and with image libraries that accept RGBA buffers.

items.title: SVG
items.text:
render_svg_node, render_svg_html, render_svg_template, and render_svg_compiled return an SVG document string:

from takumi_py import Renderer

svg = Renderer().render_svg_html(
    '<div class="card">Hello</div>',
    stylesheets=[".card { width: 1200px; height: 630px; color: black; }"],
    width=1200,
    height=630,
)

SVG output takes the viewport, font_size, time_ms, images, keyframes, font families, and lang. Encoder settings, device_pixel_ratio, dithering, and debug borders apply only to raster output.

items.title: Measurement
items.text:
measure_node, measure_html, and measure_compiled run layout without drawing and return a MeasuredNode tree:

from takumi_py import Renderer

measured = Renderer().measure_node(
    {
        "type": "container",
        "style": {"width": "240px", "height": "120px"},
        "children": [{"type": "text", "text": "Hello"}],
    },
    width=None,
    height=None,
)

print(measured.width, measured.height)
for run in measured.runs:
    print(run.text, run.x, run.y, run.width, run.height)

Each MeasuredNode carries its width, height, a 2D affine transform, its children, and the MeasuredTextRun values for the text it lays out. Measurement reports exact layout sizes; raster output snaps boxes to whole pixels as it paints.

See the runnable examples/render_options_measure.py example.

items.title: Rendering model
items.text:
Renderer follows one pipeline regardless of the source representation:

flowchart LR
    A["Node tree"] --> C["Compile"]
    B["HTML + stylesheets"] --> P["Parse"] --> C
    T["Jinja template"] --> B
    C --> D["Compiled node"]
    D --> L["Layout"]
    L --> M["Measurement"]
    L --> R["Raster image"]
    L --> S["SVG"]
    L --> N["Animation"]

This page covers the stages every input shares: choosing an input, compiling it, and configuring a render. HTML and CSS covers parsing, and Output formats covers what a render produces.

items.text: Input Entry points Guide Node tree render_node, measure_node, render_svg_node Node trees HTML render_html, measure_html, render_svg_html HTML and CSS Jinja template render_template, render_svg_template, TemplateRenderer Jinja templates Compiled node render_compiled, measure_compiled, render_svg_compiled Compile and reuse Scene sequence render_animation, render_sequence_at_time Animation

items.title: Node trees
items.text:
A node tree is a mapping with a type of "container", "text", or "image". Styles use camel-cased CSS property names, and containers nest children:

from takumi_py import Renderer

png = Renderer().render_node(
    {
        "type": "container",
        "style": {
            "width": "320px",
            "height": "160px",
            "display": "flex",
            "alignItems": "center",
            "justifyContent": "center",
            "backgroundColor": "white",
        },
        "children": [
            {"type": "text", "text": "Hello", "style": {"fontSize": "48px"}},
        ],
    },
    width=320,
    height=160,
)

Every node also accepts className, id, tagName, and attributes for selectors, tw for Tailwind classes, and dir and lang metadata. TextNode, ImageNode, and ContainerNode describe these shapes for type checkers.

Pass validate=True to a node entry point to check the mapping in Python before it reaches the native decoder. Validation raises NodeValidationError; without it, a malformed node raises NodeDecodeError from the decoder.

items.title: Compile and reuse
items.text:
For one render, call render_node or render_html directly. When the same content is rendered repeatedly, move parsing and stylesheet compilation out of the hot path:

from takumi_py import Renderer

renderer = Renderer()
compiled = renderer.compile_node({"type": "text", "text": "Reusable"})
stylesheet = renderer.compile_stylesheet("span { font-size: 32px; }")

png = renderer.render_compiled(
    compiled,
    stylesheets=[stylesheet],
    width=320,
    height=160,
)

compile_html returns a CompiledHtml bundle rather than a bare CompiledNode. Pass its node and stylesheets separately to the compiled APIs, and compile any document-level CSS before adding it to that stylesheet tuple:

from takumi_py import Renderer

renderer = Renderer()
compiled = renderer.compile_html('<div class="card">Reusable HTML</div>')
stylesheets = (
    *compiled.stylesheets,
    renderer.compile_stylesheet(
        ".card { width: 320px; height: 160px; color: black; }"
    ),
)

png = renderer.render_compiled(
    compiled.node,
    stylesheets=stylesheets,
    width=320,
    height=160,
)

Do not pass the CompiledHtml wrapper itself to render_compiled or measure_compiled; those methods accept CompiledNode.

items.title: Render options
items.text:
Every render setting is a keyword argument. RenderOptions groups the same settings into one reusable value:

from takumi_py import RenderOptions, Renderer

options = RenderOptions(
    width=None,
    height=None,
    format="raw",
    device_pixel_ratio=2.0,
    dithering="ordered-bayer",
)

raw = Renderer().render_node(
    {
        "type": "container",
        "style": {
            "width": "240px",
            "height": "120px",
            "backgroundColor": "white",
        },
    },
    options=options,
)

An explicit keyword argument overrides the matching RenderOptions field for that call, so render_node(node, options=options, format="png") keeps every other field of options. The binding still rejects contradictory combinations, such as a lossy quality together with lossless=True.

items.title: Viewport
items.text: The default viewport is 1200×630. Pass width=None or height=None to infer that dimension from layout. Fix both dimensions when output must be repeatable across calls.

items.title: Parameter contracts
items.text:
The native boundary validates values before rendering:

Parameter Contract width, height None for layout inference, otherwise a positive integer font_size Finite number greater than zero device_pixel_ratio Finite number greater than zero time_ms Non-negative integer render-level lang None or a valid BCP-47 language tag quality Integer from 0 through 100 lossless Supported only for WebP; lossless=True cannot be combined with quality dithering "none" or "ordered-bayer"; "floyd-steinberg" is a deprecated alias of "ordered-bayer"

Invalid numeric values and contradictory encoder options raise ValueError. Format names the binding does not recognize raise the format or animation exception described in the exception reference.

See the runnable examples/render_node.py and examples/render_options_measure.py examples.

items.title: Fonts and images
items.text:
The renderer never fetches resources

Read external resources into bytes in application code and pass them explicitly at the rendering boundary. This keeps networking, authentication, retries, and persistent caching outside the renderer.

items.title: Images
items.text:
Image nodes refer to images by src. Supply the bytes for each src through the per-render images option:

from pathlib import Path

from takumi_py import ImageResource, Renderer

renderer = Renderer()
png = renderer.render_node(
    {"type": "image", "src": "memory://logo", "width": 128, "height": 128},
    width=128,
    height=128,
    images=[
        ImageResource(
            "memory://logo",
            Path("logo.svg").read_bytes(),
            cache="none",
        )
    ],
)

ImageResource.cache accepts "auto" or "none" and is forwarded to the renderer's resource cache. The tuple shorthand ("memory://logo", data) remains supported and uses "auto". Images embedded as data: URIs need no resource at all.

items.title: Raw RGBA pixels
items.text:
Use RawRgbaImage when pixels are already decoded as row-major RGBA. This avoids an image codec round trip:

from takumi_py import RawRgbaImage, Renderer

source: RawRgbaImage = {
    "width": 2,
    "height": 2,
    "data": bytes([255, 0, 0, 128] * 4),
}

png = Renderer().render_node(
    {"type": "image", "src": source, "width": 2, "height": 2},
    width=2,
    height=2,
)

The byte length must be exactly width * height * 4. Data uses straight alpha by default. Set premultiplied=True only for pixels whose RGB channels already include the alpha multiplication.

items.title: Fonts
items.text:
Fonts register on a renderer and stay registered for its lifetime:

from pathlib import Path

from takumi_py import FontResource, Renderer

renderer = Renderer(load_default_fonts=False)
families = renderer.register_font(
    FontResource(
        Path("Inter-Regular.woff2").read_bytes(),
        name="Inter",
        weight=400,
        style="normal",
        generic_family="sans-serif",
    )
)

png = renderer.render_node(
    {"type": "text", "text": "Hello"},
    width=320,
    height=160,
    font_families=families,
    lang="en",
)

register_font returns the family names Takumi registered. Pass that result to font_families to select a deterministic fallback stack for a render. Takumi reads TrueType, OpenType, WOFF, and WOFF2 data.

FontResource fields override what the font file declares:

Field Contract name Family name to register under; defaults to the name in the file weight Finite number from 1 through 1000; otherwise ValueError style CSS font-style syntax such as "normal", "italic", or "oblique 12deg"; otherwise FontError generic_family Generic keyword the font resolves, such as "sans-serif" or "monospace" unicode_range Inclusive codepoint ranges the font serves; see Font subsets

The bundled font is intentionally narrow

Built-in Geist is a Latin last-resort font. Register suitable fonts for non-Latin scripts, emoji, or brand glyphs; do not depend on fonts installed on the host OS.

items.title: Font subsets
items.text:
Register each subset of a family under the same name, with the unicode_range its @font-face declares. A subset serves only the codepoints in its inclusive (start, end) ranges, as in Chrome, so text picks the right file per character:

renderer.register_fonts(
    [
        FontResource(latin, name="Inter", unicode_range=[(0x0000, 0x00FF)]),
        FontResource(cyrillic, name="Inter", unicode_range=[(0x0400, 0x045F)]),
    ]
)

Each range must satisfy 0 <= start <= end <= 0x10FFFF; anything else raises ValueError. Without unicode_range, a later font registered under the same name and descriptors shadows the earlier one, as a later @font-face rule does in a browser.

FontResource.subset_of is deprecated: Takumi now only uses it as the family name, in place of name. See Upgrade to Takumi 2.17 to migrate per-subset family names.

items.title: Releasing fonts
items.text:
unregister_font(name) removes every face registered under a family, all its unicode_range subsets included, and returns whether it had any. clear_fonts() removes every registered font, including those passed to the constructor; only the bundled Geist fallback remains, and only when the renderer was created with load_default_fonts=True.

renderer.unregister_font("Inter")
renderer.clear_fonts()

items.title: Language
items.text:
The render-level lang option affects text shaping and line breaking. It must be a valid BCP-47 language tag; every render, measure, SVG, and animation entry point rejects an invalid tag with ValueError.

Render-level lang does not write a node attribute, so it does not make CSS :lang() selectors match. Set lang on the HTML element or node that establishes the language:

HTMLNode tree 
renderer.render_html(
    '<section lang="zh-Hant"><div class="headline">你好</div></section>',
    stylesheets=[
        '.headline:lang(zh-Hant) { font-family: "Noto Sans TC"; }',
    ],
)

renderer.render_node(
    {
        "type": "container",
        "lang": "ja",
        "children": [{"type": "text", "text": "こんにちは"}],
    },
    stylesheets=[':lang(ja) { font-family: "Noto Sans JP"; }'],
)

items.title: Cache budgets
items.text:
Renderer(cache_max_bytes=...) sets the byte budget shared by that renderer's decoded images, scaled image variants, SVG rasters, and related render resources. Images embedded as data: URIs decode through the same cache, so a template that inlines its logo decodes it once per renderer rather than on every render. The default is 64 MiB; pass 0 to disable retention.

Glyph masks and outlines use a separate process-wide cache with an 8 MiB default. For CJK-heavy workloads, configure it before the first render in the process:

from takumi_py import Renderer, set_glyph_cache_max_bytes

set_glyph_cache_max_bytes(32 * 1024 * 1024)
renderer = Renderer(cache_max_bytes=128 * 1024 * 1024)

Changing the glyph budget after glyph rendering begins does not resize the existing process-wide caches.

items.title: Lifecycle
items.text:
Resource Preferred lifetime API Font Renderer lifetime register_font or register_fonts; release with unregister_font or clear_fonts Image One render images=[ImageResource(...)] Compatibility APIs

load_font, load_fonts, fetched_resources, persistent_images, put_persistent_image, and clear_image_store remain only as deprecated compatibility shims from the 0.2 line and emit DeprecationWarning. New code should pass images per render and use register_font or register_fonts.

See the runnable examples/render_resources.py example.

items.title: Jinja templates
items.text:
TemplateRenderer owns a filesystem-backed Jinja environment and sends rendered HTML to the Takumi parser.

from takumi_py import Renderer, TemplateRenderer


def uppercase(value: str) -> str:
    return value.upper()


configured_renderer = Renderer()
renderer = TemplateRenderer(
    "templates",
    filters={"uppercase": uppercase},
    renderer=configured_renderer,
)

png = renderer.render(
    "card.html.jinja",
    {"title": "takumi-py"},
    stylesheets=[
        ".card { width: 1200px; height: 630px; color: white; background: #111827; }",
    ],
    width=1200,
    height=630,
)

The template can use {{ title | uppercase }} directly. The render_template_to_html helper accepts the same filters mapping when the caller needs an HTML string rather than image output.

items.title: Inject a complete Jinja environment
items.text:
The filesystem-backed environment is a convenience default, not a restricted Jinja surface. Inject an existing jinja2.Environment when the application needs another loader, globals, tests, extensions, an undefined-value policy, a bytecode cache, or other native Jinja configuration:

from jinja2 import Environment, PackageLoader, StrictUndefined, select_autoescape

from takumi_py import TemplateRenderer


environment = Environment(
    loader=PackageLoader("my_app", "templates"),
    autoescape=select_autoescape(("html", "xml", "jinja")),
    undefined=StrictUndefined,
)
environment.globals["product_name"] = "My App"
environment.tests["featured"] = lambda item: item.featured

renderer = TemplateRenderer(
    environment=environment,
    filters={"currency": lambda value: f"${value:,.2f}"},
)

renderer.environment is the exact injected instance. filters are updated on that instance before the first template is loaded. render_template_to_html also accepts environment=.... In both APIs, template_dir and environment are mutually exclusive so that one template-loading source cannot silently shadow another.

items.title: Inject a configured renderer
items.text:
Pass an existing Renderer to TemplateRenderer when templates must share registered fonts or other renderer-owned state. Configure the renderer first, then inject that same instance:

from pathlib import Path

from takumi_py import FontResource, Renderer, TemplateRenderer


def uppercase(value: str) -> str:
    return value.upper()


configured_renderer = Renderer(load_default_fonts=False)
families = configured_renderer.register_font(
    FontResource(
        Path("Inter-Regular.woff2").read_bytes(),
        name="Inter",
        generic_family="sans-serif",
    )
)
renderer = TemplateRenderer(
    "templates",
    filters={"uppercase": uppercase},
    renderer=configured_renderer,
)
png = renderer.render(
    "card.html.jinja",
    {"title": "takumi-py"},
    stylesheets=[".card { width: 1200px; height: 630px; }"],
    font_families=families,
    width=1200,
    height=630,
)

items.title: Responsibility boundaries
items.text:
flowchart LR
    T["Template + context"] --> J["Jinja environment"]
    J --> H["HTML"]
    H --> P["Takumi parser"]
    C["Stylesheets"] --> P
    R["Fonts + images"] --> E["Render"]
    P --> E
  • Configure filters, globals, tests, and extensions before the first render. Jinja does not guarantee predictable behavior when an environment is mutated after a template has already been loaded.
  • Templates generate HTML. Supply images through render inputs. Register custom fonts on an injected renderer as shown above and follow the resource guide.
  • Keep CSS in explicit stylesheets inputs so the template layer does not own render configuration.
  • Jinja autoescape is enabled by default for HTML, XML, and Jinja files. A caller-owned environment retains its own autoescape policy.

Custom filters execute application code

Treat filter functions and template directories as trusted application inputs. Autoescape protects interpolated markup; it does not sandbox Python filter code.

See the runnable examples/render_template.py example and its card.html.jinja template.

items.title: Maintainers
items.text:
This section defines repository workflows. It is not part of the binding's public API.

  • Development

    Environment setup, checks, the Takumi submodule, and the native extension.

    Development

  • Documentation

    Languages, information architecture, content ownership, local builds, and versioning.

    Documentation

  • Releasing

    Version contracts, the CI release graph, external controls, and recovery paths.

    Releasing

Keeping maintainer workflows separate from user guides prevents repository operations from being mistaken for product contracts.

items.title: Prepare the environment
items.text:
git submodule update --init --recursive
uv sync --all-groups --all-extras
uv run maturin develop

The Rust toolchain is pinned by rust-toolchain.toml. Project lock files manage Python, Rust, and documentation dependencies; do not patch the repository environment with ad hoc pip install commands.

items.title: Common checks
items.text:
make check
make docs-build
prek run --all-files
prek run actionlint --all-files --hook-stage=manual

make check runs Ruff, ty, mypy.stubtest for the native extension, pytest, Rustfmt, and Clippy. The documentation build runs separately because it uses the docs dependency group: it checks that the Chinese pages mirror the English source, then builds both languages strictly, treating warnings as failures. The manual Actionlint stage validates embedded workflow shell scripts in addition to the normal repository hooks.

items.title: Tests
items.text:
The pytest suite lives in tests/ and runs in parallel through make test:

Module Covers test_render_node.py, test_render_html.py, test_render_template.py The node, HTML, and template entry points test_html_adapter.py, test_inline_style.py HTML parsing and inline styles test_core_binding_features.py Options, fonts, images, caches, measurement, SVG, and animation test_takumi_core_fixtures.py Every upstream HTML fixture under takumilib/takumi/tests/fixtures-html renders test_examples.py Every script in examples/ runs and writes its output test_typing_surface.py The documented public Renderer surface and native typing artifacts

items.title: Distribution contract
items.text:
Build the current platform wheel and sdist through the same local contract used by CI:

make build-artifacts

The target checks metadata and archive contents, installs the wheel in a temporary environment outside the checkout, rebuilds a wheel from the sdist, and runs the native rendering smoke against both paths. Use make verify-artifacts DIST_DIR=/path/to/dist to validate an existing local pair.

items.title: Native extension
items.text:
The Python package loads from python/, and the native module is named takumi_py._core. Rebuild it after changing Rust binding code:

uv run maturin develop

Rebuild before testing binding changes

Running Python tests without rebuilding can accidentally exercise a stale native artifact from the previous compilation.

items.title: Takumi submodule
items.text:
Takumi is an explicit source dependency of this repository. Pin takumilib to the upstream release commit that a takumi@X.Y.Z tag points to, never to a branch tip or a local merge:

git -C takumilib fetch origin --tags
git -C takumilib checkout --detach 'takumi@2.17.1^{commit}'
cargo update -w

An upgrade must check:

  • The submodule revision and Cargo.lock
  • Version constraints for takumi and takumi-core
  • Deprecations in the upstream API: Clippy runs with -D warnings, so a deprecated call fails the build. Adopt the replacement that the Node binding in takumilib/takumi-napi uses, and surface the change as a Python DeprecationWarning
  • New upstream capabilities worth exposing, by comparing the Node binding's surface with Renderer
  • That the build stays within the toolchain in rust-toolchain.toml: rust-version keeps the resolver on compatible crates, and running cargo +1.91.0 clippy --locked --all-targets through rustup confirms it
  • That the HTML fixtures read by tests/test_takumi_core_fixtures.py still exist under takumilib/takumi/tests/fixtures-html
  • Whether the source distribution can still rebuild a wheel in isolation
  • Whether assets referenced by the binding under takumilib/assets changed

Upstream's [patch.crates-io] forks of fontations and harfrust apply only inside the Takumi workspace. This crate builds against the crates.io releases, so a patch upstream adds is not inherited.

The repository checkout is not an sdist dependency

Never hide missing distribution files by reading them from the surrounding checkout. The CI sdist smoke test must build and run entirely from the isolated source archive.

items.title: Languages
items.text:
The documentation is bilingual. American English is the primary language, and Simplified Chinese mirrors it page for page:

Language Source Configuration Published at English docs/en/ zensical.toml Site root Simplified Chinese docs/zh/ zensical.zh.toml zh/
  • The English page is the source of truth. Change it first, then update the Chinese page in the same change so the two never describe different behavior.
  • Both trees hold the same pages at the same paths, and both configurations declare the same navigation. Code samples are identical; only prose, headings, and navigation titles are translated.
  • The API reference renders English docstrings on both sites. Chinese reference pages translate only the prose around the generated signatures.
  • make docs-build runs .github/scripts/check-docs-i18n.py before the strict builds. It fails when a page lacks its counterpart, when the navigation of the two languages diverges, or when the two configurations differ outside their language-specific keys.

items.title: English style
items.text: Write in American English: "behavior", "color", "initialize", "license" as a noun and a verb. Use the second person and the present tense, and name the API a sentence is about.

items.title: Chinese terminology
items.text:
Keep API names, parameters, and literals in code font and untranslated. Translate the recurring concepts consistently:

English 中文 renderer 渲染器 node tree 节点树 compiled node 已编译节点 stylesheet 样式表 viewport 视口 raster output 位图输出 measurement 测量 font family 字体族 fallback 回退 subset 子集 golden image 基准图 deprecation warning 弃用警告 source distribution (sdist) 源码分发包（sdist）

Give every Chinese heading the English page's anchor, such as ## 字体子集 { #font-subsets }, so in-page links match across both languages.

items.title: Information architecture
items.text:
Each language tree is divided by audience and task:

docs/en/ and docs/zh/
├── getting-started/  # Shortest path to a successful render
├── guides/           # Task-oriented explanations and composition
├── reference/        # Exact contracts, support matrix, generated API
├── migration/        # Behavioral and required changes across core upgrades
└── maintainers/      # Repository workflows and release operations

Before adding a page, decide whether it answers how to complete a task, what the exact contract is, what changed during an upgrade, or how to maintain the repository. A page that fits none of these categories probably mixes responsibilities and should be split first.

items.title: Content ownership
items.text:
• README.md and its Chinese counterpart README.zh-CN.md provide the project overview, installation, a minimal example, and links into the documentation. They do not repeat guide content.
  • docs/*/guides/ owns usage behavior. Each topic has one home; other pages link to it instead of restating it.
  • docs/*/reference/api/ renders source signatures with mkdocstrings and does not copy parameter tables by hand.
  • Runnable examples live in examples/, where tests/test_examples.py executes them. Guides link to them rather than embedding complete scripts.
  • CHANGELOG.md records release facts in English: curated notes under [Unreleased], which make changelog dates and completes with the release's commits and contributors. Each released section becomes the GitHub Release notes. Migration pages explain cross-version decisions and required changes.
  • Release operations, including versioned documentation deployment, live only in maintainers/releasing.md.

items.title: Authoring locally
items.text:
Preview one language at a time:

make docs-serve
make docs-serve-zh

The header's language button, next to the light and dark toggle, opens the same page, version, and anchor in the other language. It is a theme override in docs/overrides/partials/alternate.html that swaps the versionless site_url of the two extra.alternate entries, so it follows the published layout, the site root and zh/, and only switches on the deployed site. Run the same checks and strict builds used by CI before submitting a change:

make docs-build

zensical.toml and zensical.zh.toml live at the repository root. Explicit nav is part of the public information architecture: update it in both files whenever a page is added, moved, or removed.

items.title: Available authoring components
items.text:
Use framework components when they improve comprehension:

Need Component Compare alternative inputs or commands Linked content tabs Surface a warning without breaking the main flow Admonition or collapsible detail Present peer destinations on an index page Card grid Explain a pipeline or state transition Mermaid diagram Explain one line without interrupting a runnable example Code annotation

Avoid decorative components that add no information hierarchy.

items.title: Icons
items.text:
Icons come from the sets bundled with Zensical: Lucide, Material Design, FontAwesome, Octicons, and Simple Icons. Both configurations enable them through attr_list and pymdownx.emoji with Zensical's to_svg generator and twemoji index, which inline each icon as SVG; keep those settings identical in both files. See the Zensical icons and emojis guide for the syntax.

  • In front matter and in the configuration, reference an icon by its path under .icons without the extension, such as icon: lucide/rocket or repo = "fontawesome/brands/github".
  • In Markdown, replace each / in that path with - and wrap it in colons, such as :material-rocket-launch:. Add classes with an attribute list.
  • Section index pages set a Lucide page icon in front matter. Each card in a card grid opens with an icon marked { .lg .middle } and links onward with :octicons-arrow-right-24:. Brand logos come from Simple Icons, such as :simple-jinja:.
  • A Chinese page uses the same icons, attributes, and page icon as its English source.
  • A misspelled shortcode renders as literal text and does not fail the strict build. Confirm the icon exists under zensical/templates/.icons/ in the installed package, because the bundled sets can lag behind the icon sites, then check the rendered page.
  • The documentation does not use emoji shortcodes such as :smile:. Twemoji renders them as images loaded from a CDN rather than as inline SVG.

items.title: Versioning
items.text: The site uses the Zensical-compatible mike fork. Version preparation runs from the verified release tag at the end of the automatic release pipeline. The generated gh-pages branch is persistent version state rather than the Pages publishing source; the release workflow exports it as a Pages artifact and deploys it through the github-pages environment. English versions live at the branch root and Chinese versions under zh/, each with its own versions.json, so each site's version selector lists its own deployments. Every push to main also deploys its docs as the dev version, as the documentation preview describes; ordinary documentation builds for pull requests validate the site without updating either destination.

items.title: Releasing
items.text: A version change on main drives every normal release. Maintainers do not build artifacts, create tags, or deploy documentation by hand; automation only processes a version that satisfies both the version contract and the exact-commit gates.

items.title: Prepare the release commit
items.text:
A release commit must satisfy every part of this contract:

  • The project versions in pyproject.toml and the root Cargo.toml match exactly.
  • The project version strictly increases over the first parent on main and uses the canonical PEP 440 form.
  • uv.lock and Cargo.lock are up to date and pass the locked checks.
  • CHANGELOG.md has a dated section for the version, written by make changelog.
  • make check, make docs-build, and every Prek hook pass.

Update versions with the project tools rather than editing the version fields directly, then write the changelog entry:

uv version 0.3.0 --no-sync
cargo set-version 0.3.0
make changelog

items.title: Changelog entry
items.text:
Curate user-facing notes under ## [Unreleased] in CHANGELOG.md as changes land, in Keep a Changelog sections. make changelog turns them into the release entry:

  • It dates [Unreleased] as the project version and opens a new, empty [Unreleased] above it.
  • It appends a Commits list that git-changelog builds from the conventional commits since the previous tag: breaking changes first, then one group per commit type, each commit linked by its short hash.
  • It ends the entry with a link to the full diff and a Contributors line that @-mentions every author, co-author, and committer, except GitHub's own merge committer.

Logins come from GitHub noreply addresses, or from gh api for other emails, so run the target with gh authenticated. Passing --offline to .github/scripts/changelog.py release lists those people by name instead. Preview the entry with make changelog-preview VERSION=0.3.0, edit its curated part if needed, and commit it with the version bump.

The release workflow publishes that section verbatim as the GitHub Release notes. Merge the release pull request with a merge commit: a squash or rebase merge rewrites the hashes the entry links to.

After the commit merges into main, Check · Build and test, Check · Docs, and Check · Lint each verify that same commit. Release · Tag waits for all three workflows to succeed, confirms the version, lock files, changelog, and ancestry on main, creates an annotated v0.3.0 tag on the commit, and dispatches Release · Publish exactly once.

Normal releases no longer create tags by hand

The automatic tag is part of the exact-commit gate. A manual tag skips the gate aggregation and is reserved for recovery an administrator has explicitly approved; do not run git tag or Release · Publish directly for a normal release.

items.title: Automatic release pipeline
items.text:
flowchart TD
    M["Version commit lands on main"] --> C["Check · Build and test: tests + four platform wheels + sdist + abi3"]
    M --> D["Check · Docs: strict build"]
    M --> K["Check · Lint: repository + Actions lint"]
    C --> T["Release · Tag: aggregate the same source SHA"]
    D --> T
    K --> T
    T --> V["Check version, locks, changelog, and main ancestry"]
    V --> G["Create annotated tag and dispatch Release · Publish"]
    G --> B["Re-check and build four wheels and one sdist"]
    B --> A["Verify metadata, licenses, platforms, and isolated installs"]
    A --> P["Generate provenance and publish to PyPI"]
    P --> H["Verify PyPI filenames and SHA-256 digests"]
    H --> R["Publish or recover the GitHub Release"]
    R --> X["Prepare versioned docs from the release tag"]
    X --> Y["Deploy through a GitHub Pages artifact and OIDC"]

A release build produces four cp311-abi3 wheels, for Linux x86_64, Linux aarch64, macOS arm64, and Windows x64, plus one sdist. The verification layer:

  1. Checks the complete artifact set, package metadata, licenses, ABI and platform tags, and the bundled-font boundary.
  2. Installs each artifact into a temporary virtual environment outside the repository and runs a rendering smoke test, so nothing imports from the checkout by accident.
  3. Rebuilds a wheel from the sdist and runs the same isolated smoke test on the result.
  4. Generates GitHub build provenance for the files that are finally uploaded.
  5. Uploads to PyPI through Trusted Publishing. A rerun may skip files that already exist, but the result must then match the complete file set and SHA-256 digests in the PyPI JSON exactly.
  6. Publishes the GitHub Release, with the version's CHANGELOG.md section as its notes, only after the PyPI check succeeds. An existing published Release only allows an idempotent rerun with matching digests, and an existing draft can be recovered with the artifacts this run verified, taking the changelog notes.
  7. Updates both documentation languages from the same release tag with .github/scripts/deploy-docs.py, which runs mike: English at the site root and Simplified Chinese under the zh/ prefix, each with its own versions.json. A tag that predates the Chinese site deploys English only. Only a release no older than the newest released version moves latest, and concurrent writes to the gh-pages branch, which stores the version state, retry a bounded number of times.
  8. Exports the full static tree from the current gh-pages, uploads a standard github-pages artifact, and deploys it through OIDC to the protected github-pages environment.

items.title: Documentation preview
items.text:
Preview · Docs publishes main as the dev documentation version. After every successful Check · Docs run for a push to main, it builds that exact commit in both languages with .github/scripts/deploy-docs.py dev and deploys GitHub Pages, so a documentation change on main is online within minutes.

  • dev (main) heads the version selector, above the releases, at /takumi-py/dev/ and /takumi-py/zh/dev/. latest and the site root stay on the newest release.
  • A newer commit's preview cancels one that is still running.
  • Release and preview Pages deployments share the github-pages concurrency group, and each exports the gh-pages tip when it deploys, so neither drops the other's versions.

To check release artifacts locally, run:

make build-artifacts

The target builds the current platform's wheel and sdist, runs the Twine metadata check, and verifies the wheel and the sdist rebuild path in isolated environments. DIST_SMOKE_PYTHON selects the Python version the smoke test uses.

items.title: External repository settings
items.text:
Repository files cannot enable the following controls; an administrator configures them on GitHub and PyPI:

  • Protect main, requiring at least Check · Build and test / Required checks, Check · Docs / Build documentation, and Check · Lint / Run repository hooks, plus code-owner review of the release automation.
  • Allow the GitHub Actions GITHUB_TOKEN to receive the write permissions the workflows declare. If release tags are protected, configure a controlled bypass for Release · Tag.
  • Configure required reviewers on the release environment.
  • Bind the PyPI Trusted Publisher to owner BalconyJH, repository takumi-py, workflow publish.yml, and environment release.
  • Set the GitHub Pages source to GitHub Actions, and let the github-pages environment deploy only from main, for the dev preview, and trusted v* release tags.
  • Enable immutable GitHub Releases; the workflow only verifies digests of a published Release and never rewrites it.
  • Keep the weekly Dependabot updates for GitHub Actions, and route SHA pin updates through the same gates.

items.title: Failure recovery
items.text:
A gate failed before the tag was createdThe tag exists, but Publish did not succeedPyPI already accepted some or all filesThe GitHub Release or docs deployment failed

Fix the problem and merge the fix into main. Because the fix commit may keep the parent's version, automatic detection will not treat it as a version change again. Run Release · Tag by hand from the current main, passing the full 40-character source_sha of the current commit. Recovery mode only accepts the current main and still requires all three exact-commit workflows to succeed.

Run Release · Publish by hand from the matching tag or the default branch, passing the same release_tag. Do not create a replacement tag or move the existing one.

Rerun Release · Publish for the same tag. The upload step uses skip-existing, and the digest check that follows confirms that existing files are the ones this run built. Missing files wait for PyPI metadata to converge; a digest mismatch fails at once.

Run Release · Publish again for the same tag. A published Release is reused only when its file set and digests match exactly, and a draft can be recovered from the verified artifacts. Docs preparation reads the remote gh-pages again and retries conflicts, and the Pages deployment that follows reuses the static artifact uploaded by the same run.

Never rewrite published artifacts

PyPI files, published GitHub Releases, and release tags are immutable inputs. Any digest mismatch should stop the release for investigation, rather than a force push, a replacement version, or an overwritten file.

items.title: Migration
items.text:
Migration guides describe behavioral changes and required code changes between Takumi core versions. They do not duplicate the commit-by-commit record in the changelog.

  • Takumi v2

    Resource ownership, HTML parsing, font descriptors, language behavior, and output changes.

    Open migration guide

  • Takumi 2.17

    Font subsets by unicode_range, deprecated subset_of and Floyd–Steinberg dithering, animation frame-rate limits, and Chrome-aligned rendering.

    Open migration guide

Read both migration guidance and release history

During the testing stage, also review the changelog entries between your current and target versions.

items.title: Upgrade to Takumi 2.17
items.text: The next takumi-py release moves the native renderer from Takumi 2.5.4 to 2.17.1. The Python API stays compatible, but a few inputs change meaning and Takumi's output moves closer to Chrome's.

items.title: Expect pixel changes
items.text:
Takumi 2.6 through 2.17 port more of Chromium's layout and paint behavior: text and inline layout, line heights, text decorations, filters and backdrop-filter, backgrounds, borders, outlines, box-shadow, tables, and CSS paint order. An image that was correct under 2.5 can shift by a few pixels or change where it previously diverged from a browser.

Regenerate golden images after upgrading, and compare a suspicious difference with Chrome before treating it as a binding regression. The upstream Takumi changelog lists every rendering change.

items.title: Required changes
items.text: Before After Why One FontResource(name="Inter-latin", subset_of="Inter") per subset FontResource(name="Inter", unicode_range=[...]) for every subset subset_of now only sets the family name font_families=["Inter-latin", "Inter-cyrillic"] font_families=["Inter"] Subsets no longer register under their own names dithering="floyd-steinberg" dithering="ordered-bayer" Takumi removed error diffusion; the old name is an alias render_animation(..., fps=60, format="gif") fps of at most 50 for GIF, 90 for WebP and APNG Higher rates now raise ValueError

items.title: Font subsets
items.text:
Register each subset of a family under the family's own name, with the codepoint ranges its @font-face declares. Takumi serves each codepoint from the subset whose range covers it:

Takumi 2.17Takumi 2.5 
from pathlib import Path

from takumi_py import FontResource, Renderer

renderer = Renderer()
renderer.register_fonts(
    [
        FontResource(
            Path("Inter-Latin.woff2").read_bytes(),
            name="Inter",
            unicode_range=[(0x0000, 0x00FF)],
        ),
        FontResource(
            Path("Inter-Cyrillic.woff2").read_bytes(),
            name="Inter",
            unicode_range=[(0x0400, 0x045F)],
        ),
    ]
)

renderer.register_fonts(
    [
        FontResource(latin, name="Inter-latin", subset_of="Inter"),
        FontResource(cyrillic, name="Inter-cyrillic", subset_of="Inter"),
    ]
)

subset_of still works, but it emits a DeprecationWarning and takes precedence over name, so register_font returns the subset_of value. Without unicode_range, a later font registered under the same name and descriptors shadows the earlier one, as a later @font-face rule does in a browser.

items.title: Behavior changes
items.text:
• <img> without a src attribute parses as an empty box sized by its width and height, as Chrome draws it. It used to raise HtmlParseError.
  • compile_stylesheet accepts CSS that Takumi 2.5 rejected, such as text-decoration: none. Values Takumi still cannot parse raise StyleSheetError as before.
  • The renderer resource cache defaults to 64 MiB instead of 16 MiB. Images embedded as data: URIs now decode through it, once per renderer.
  • render_animation streams frames into the encoder, so it holds one raw frame at a time. The encoded bytes are the same as before.

items.title: New APIs
items.text:
• FontResource.unicode_range limits the codepoints a font serves.
  • Renderer.unregister_font(name) releases a family with all of its subsets.
  • Renderer.clear_fonts() releases every registered font, leaving only the bundled fallback when the renderer loads it.

See Fonts and images for usage.

items.title: Upgrade checklist
items.text:
• Replace subset_of with one family name plus unicode_range per subset.
  • Drop per-subset family names from font_families and CSS font-family.
  • Replace dithering="floyd-steinberg" with "ordered-bayer".
  • Keep fps within 50 for GIF and 90 for WebP and APNG.
  • Run the test suite with -W error::DeprecationWarning to find deprecated calls.
  • Regenerate and review golden images.

items.title: Migrate to Takumi v2
items.text: Takumi v2 replaces implicit renderer-level resource context with explicit resource inputs and maps the Python binding more directly to core.

items.title: Resource APIs
items.text:
Previous interface Preferred interface fetched_resources Pass images=[ImageResource(...)] to each render load_font / load_fonts register_font / register_fonts Persistent image APIs Prefer per-render images

The old interfaces remain temporarily as deprecated compatibility shims. New code should use the explicit model directly.

items.title: HTML and stylesheets
items.text: HTML parsing now lives in Takumi's Rust parser. HTML render, measure, SVG, and template calls all receive document-level CSS explicitly through stylesheets=[...], and inline style attributes are parsed with the HTML. Use HtmlOptions to customize parser presets, the Tailwind attribute, or the depth limit. See HTML and CSS.

items.title: Fonts and language
items.text:
• FontResource accepts name, weight, style, generic_family, and unicode_range descriptors. A weight override must be finite and within 1 through 1000. Since Takumi 2.17, register each subset of a family under one name with its own unicode_range; see Upgrade to Takumi 2.17.
  • register_font(s) returns the actual family names, which can be passed to render calls as font_families.
  • Render-level lang affects shaping and line breaking; CSS :lang() still depends on an HTML or node attribute. Invalid BCP-47 render-level tags raise ValueError.
  • The built-in fallback is now Latin Geist as a last resort. Caller-provided fonts participate first in normal fallback.

items.title: Images and URLs
items.text: ImageResource.cache maps directly to the Takumi image cache hint for per-render, constructor, and deprecated persistent images. Image nodes also accept decoded RawRgbaImage pixels. CompiledNode.resource_urls() reports HTTP(S) image and style references, but it does not download them or report already supplied memory:// bytes. See Fonts and images.

items.title: Animation and output
items.text:
• Pass structured keyframes through keyframes= or RenderOptions(keyframes=...).
  • WebP defaults to lossless when neither quality nor lossless is specified, and quality together with lossless=True is rejected.
  • Render SVG with render_svg_node, render_svg_html, render_svg_template, or render_svg_compiled.

items.title: Migration checklist
items.text:
• Replace implicit fetched resources with explicit ImageResource inputs.
  • Replace deprecated font loaders with registration APIs.
  • Pass document-level CSS through stylesheets.
  • Register fonts for every script used by the rendered text.
  • Exercise raster, SVG, measurement, and animation output used by the application.

Layout changes after migration

Check Web-platform defaults first: position, border and outline widths, transform-origin, object-position, and SVG currentColor inheritance.

items.text:
Reference pages define exact support and API contracts. For decision-oriented explanations and complete examples, start with the guides.

  • Support matrix

    Runtime versions, published wheels, formats, resource ownership, and exclusions.

    Support matrix

  • Exceptions

  • Renderer API

    Renderer

  • Supporting types

    Render options, resources, nodes, results, and template entry points.

    Options · Types · HTML · Templates

Import from the public package

_core is the native extension implementation module. Application code should import from takumi_py and must not treat _core as a compatibility boundary.

items.title: Exceptions
items.text:
All public exception classes can be imported from takumi_py.

Exception Typical boundary TakumiError Base class exposed by the binding NodeValidationError Python input does not match the typed node structure NodeDecodeError A native node or measurement result cannot be decoded HtmlParseError The HTML parser rejects its input StyleSheetError CSS or keyframe compilation fails FontError Font description, parsing, or registration fails ResourceError An image or another resource is invalid or undecodable RenderError Layout or rendering of an image, SVG, or animation frame fails AnimationError Animation encoding fails, or the animation format or raw frames are invalid UnsupportedFormatError The requested output format is unsupported

Catch the narrowest useful exception. Catch TakumiError only at an API boundary that intentionally translates every binding failure into an application-level error:

from takumi_py import FontError, FontResource, Renderer

try:
    Renderer().register_font(FontResource(b"not a font"))
except FontError as error:
    raise ValueError("invalid configured font") from error

Preserve the original error

Do not catch Exception and discard the cause. Native error messages carry the context required to locate invalid render inputs.

items.title: Resource model
items.text:
• One Latin Geist last-resort font is compiled into the extension.
  • Callers provide all other font and image bytes. Fonts register per renderer, can be split into unicode_range subsets, and can be released again.
  • resource_urls() discovers URLs without accessing the network.
  • Images accept a per-render cache hint; the binding does not provide an HTTP client.
  • Each renderer exposes a resource-cache budget; glyph caches use a separate process-wide budget configured before first use.

items.title: Explicit exclusions
items.text:
• Playwright or browser fallback
  • Remote resource fetching
  • AbortSignal or an asynchronous cancellation protocol
  • Data URL convenience APIs
  • A Node.js sidecar
  • Direct mappings of Takumi's internal layout, cache, or glyph implementation types

Compose infrastructure at the application boundary

These exclusions keep binding responsibilities aligned with Takumi core. Compose remote fetching, persistent caching, or task cancellation in the application instead of reaching through renderer internals.

  1. A source build requires Rust 1.91 or later, a Python development environment, and the native dependencies of the target platform. ↩

items.title: HTML parsing
items.text:
parse_html is the standalone Rust-backed HTML parser. It returns a ParsedHtml bundle containing the compiled node and any compiled stylesheets associated with the parse result. Pass those fields separately to a compiled renderer API:

from takumi_py import Renderer, parse_html

parsed = parse_html("<article>Hello</article>")
png = Renderer().render_compiled(
    parsed.node,
    stylesheets=parsed.stylesheets,
    width=320,
    height=160,
)

Use HtmlOptions to select parser presets, map Tailwind classes from another attribute, or cap nesting depth. Document-level CSS remains an explicit render input; compile it with Renderer.compile_stylesheet before passing it to a compiled API. HTML compilation is performed directly by the native parser; HTML entry points do not have a separate Python-side validate switch. See HTML and CSS for the full parsing behavior.

The Python type layer defines node inputs, measurement results, and animation scenes.

AnimationScene.duration_ms and RawAnimationFrame.duration_ms must be positive. Raw animation frames also require positive dimensions and exactly width * height * 4 RGBA bytes.

RawRgbaImage describes decoded row-major RGBA pixels used as an ImageNode.src. Its byte length follows the same width * height * 4 contract.
